newsitem.title: USA: Boeing work force tops forecast at 120,000.
newsitem.headline: Boeing work force tops forecast at 120,000.

text.p: Boeing Co.'s work force has expanded to more than 120,000, well in excess of the company's latest forecast as the world's biggest airplane manufacturer scrambles to meet rising demand, an official said Friday.
The company is continuing to hire, ensuring that year-end employment will be well over the 118,350 forecast by the company less than two months ago, Boeing spokesman Paul Binder said.
The company's work force already has risen some 14 percent from 105,185 at the end of last year but is still far below a peak of 166,000 in 1989.
In April the company forecast it would add 8,200 jobs this year, but that figure was raised by an additional 5,000 in August.

Binder said the company was meeting internal objectives, adding that the forecasts are issued mainly to help planners in Washington state, where it is the biggest private employer by far with more than 80,000 workers.

After years of painful cutbacks, Boeing has announced several production rate increases this year in response to airline orders that are running high above last year's pace and are expected to continue rising.

Union workers at the company's vast Everett, Wash., assembly plant have been ordered to work some Saturday shifts to maintain an increased pace of three and a half 747 jumbo jets a month, up from just two last month.
And Machinists union District 751, which had 9,000 people on its layoff rolls at one point last year, now has only 600 people waiting to be recalled, said spokeswoman Connie Kelliher.
She said the company recalled 596 people last week, up from a recent average of 150 to 200 a week.
